summary: Backend regression for the multi-channel push notification implementation. 40/40 pytest cases PASS. Verified: (1) services/push_relay.py and services/notifications.py import cleanly with _channel_for_kind exposed. (2) _channel_for_kind correctly maps all required kinds: personal/inbox/message → messages, broadcast/broadcast_review/broadcast_sent/broadcast_rejected → broadcasts, new_booking/booking_confirmed/booking_reminder/booking_cancelled/booking_completed → appointments, video_room_ready → video_calls, note_reminder/review_request → reminders; None/''/unknown → default; case-insensitive ('BROADCAST' → broadcasts) AND prefix heuristics (booking_followup_custom → appointments, broadcast_custom_x → broadcasts, daily_med_reminder → reminders) work. (3) send_push() with EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY='placeholder' returns the exact documented contract {'sent':0,'ok':False,'reason':'no_emergent_key'} without raising; missing title/message short-circuits to 'missing_title_or_message'; empty recipients short-circuits to 'no_recipients'. (4) Core endpoints still work end-to-end: POST /api/register-push returns 200 with {registered:True, user_id, relay:{registered:False, reason:'no_emergent_key'}} confirming the DB upsert succeeds AND the relay no-ops cleanly; POST /api/messages/send happy + validation paths return non-500 (channel injection on the legacy path doesn't blow up); POST /api/broadcasts creates pending/approved row; PATCH /api/broadcasts/{id} action=approve executes the _relay_send path without throwing even with placeholder key (returns 200 or 400 'Already sent', never 500); GET /api/notifications returns 200 for both owner and patient. (5) Route count unchanged — 303 paths in openapi spec, push-related endpoints still the same 7 (/api/push/register, /api/push/heal, /api/push/fcm-errors, /api/push/diagnostics, /api/push/test, /api/register-push, /api/push/test-self). No new endpoints introduced by the channel-mapping work. EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY=placeholder is the expected dev state (not a bug — actual FCM delivery can only be validated on a real device build).
action_items: No blocking action items. Push multi-channel backend wiring is correct. Main agent may merge.
(Optional) When EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY is finally injected in production, run this same test file to confirm the contract flips to {'sent':>0, 'ok':True} for live recipients.
critical_code_review_comments: services/push_relay.py:72 — _channel_for_kind is robust: dict lookup + lowercase + startswith heuristics + 'reminder' substring fallback. Handles None and unknown kinds gracefully. Excellent defensive design.

services/push_relay.py:232-242 — Channel resolution inside send_push uses the kind arg first, then payload data.type/kind, then falls back to data-dict kind. setdefault() means caller-supplied channel_id is preserved if explicitly set (idempotent injection). Good.

services/notifications.py:176-181 — Legacy Expo-direct path now imports _channel_for_kind from services.push_relay and stamps channelId on the message envelope AND channel_id/category on data. Try/except around the import keeps the fallback safe even if push_relay later gets renamed.

services/push_relay.py:208-214 — When is_configured() is False, send_push() still writes a push_log row with note='no_emergent_key' BEFORE returning the no-op response. This preserves observability (Notifications Health panel will still show the attempt) which is correct behavior.

routers/broadcasts.py:78-89 — Routes broadcast_review and broadcast pushes through _relay_send with the right `kind=` so _channel_for_kind picks 'broadcasts'. No regression. The dev-fallback to send_expo_push_batch also gets the channel correctly (data['type']='broadcast_review' is read by the legacy path's _kind_hint logic).
